# Reachability Fixpoint & Decision Problems

This notebook walks through the **reachability fixpoint** algorithm for
deciding language emptiness, and then shows how **universality**, **inclusion**,
and **equivalence** all reduce to emptiness checks.

**Running example -- DFA that accepts words containing "aaa":**

- States: $q_0, q_1, q_2, q_3$
- $\delta(q_0,a)=q_1,\; \delta(q_0,b)=q_0,\; \delta(q_1,a)=q_2,\; \delta(q_1,b)=q_0,\; \delta(q_2,a)=q_3,\; \delta(q_2,b)=q_0,\; \delta(q_3,a)=q_3,\; \delta(q_3,b)=q_3$
- $F = \{q_3\}$

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var STEPS = [
    {
      explain: "<b>Iteration 0 &mdash; Initialise.</b> R&#x2080; = {q&#x2080;} (the initial state). No Post computed yet.",
      reached: ["q0"], newStates: ["q0"], iter: [],
      tableRows: [{i:"0", r:"{q₀}", post:"—", news:"{q₀}"}]
    },
    {
      explain: "<b>Iteration 1 &mdash; Compute Post(R&#x2080;).</b> Post({q&#x2080;}) = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;} (q&#x2080; &xrarr;b q&#x2080;, q&#x2080; &xrarr;a q&#x2081;). R&#x2081; = R&#x2080; &cup; Post(R&#x2080;) = <code>{q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;}</code>. New state: <b>q&#x2081;</b>.",
      reached: ["q0","q1"], newStates: ["q1"], iter: [],
      tableRows: [
        {i:"0", r:"{q₀}", post:"—", news:"{q₀}"},
        {i:"1", r:"{q₀;, q₁}", post:"{q₀;, q₁}", news:"{q₁}", hl:true}
      ]
    },
    {
      explain: "<b>Iteration 2 &mdash; Compute Post(R&#x2081;).</b> Post({q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;}) = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;} (adds q&#x2081; &xrarr;a q&#x2082;). R&#x2082; = <code>{q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;}</code>. New state: <b>q&#x2082;</b>.",
      reached: ["q0","q1","q2"], newStates: ["q2"], iter: [],
      tableRows: [
        {i:"0", r:"{q₀}", post:"—", news:"{q₀}"},
        {i:"1", r:"{q₀;, q₁}", post:"{q₀;, q₁}", news:"{q₁}"},
        {i:"2", r:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂}", post:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂}", news:"{q₂}", hl:true}
      ]
    },
    {
      explain: "<b>Iteration 3 &mdash; Compute Post(R&#x2082;).</b> Post({q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;}) = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;} (adds q&#x2082; &xrarr;a q&#x2083;). R&#x2083; = <code>{q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;}</code>. New state: <b>q&#x2083;</b>.",
      reached: ["q0","q1","q2","q3"], newStates: ["q3"], iter: [],
      tableRows: [
        {i:"0", r:"{q₀}", post:"—", news:"{q₀}"},
        {i:"1", r:"{q₀;, q₁}", post:"{q₀;, q₁}", news:"{q₁}"},
        {i:"2", r:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂}", post:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂}", news:"{q₂}"},
        {i:"3", r:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂;, q₃}", post:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂;, q₃}", news:"{q₃}", hl:true}
      ]
    },
    {
      explain: "<b>Iteration 4 &mdash; Compute Post(R&#x2083;).</b> Post({q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;}) = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;} = R&#x2083;. <b>FIXPOINT REACHED!</b><br><br>R* &cap; F = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;} &cap; {q&#x2083;} = {q&#x2083;} &ne; &empty; &rarr; <b>Language is NON-EMPTY.</b> Shortest witness: <code>aaa</code> (length 3, first reaching q&#x2083; at iteration 3).",
      reached: ["q0","q1","q2","q3"], newStates: [], iter: [],
      tableRows: [
        {i:"0", r:"{q₀}", post:"—", news:"{q₀}"},
        {i:"1", r:"{q₀;, q₁}", post:"{q₀;, q₁}", news:"{q₁}"},
        {i:"2", r:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂}", post:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂}", news:"{q₂}"},
        {i:"3", r:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂;, q₃}", post:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂;, q₃}", news:"{q₃}"},
        {i:"4", r:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂;, q₃}", post:"{q₀;, q₁;, q₂;, q₃}", news:"∅", hl:true}
      ]
    }
  ];

  var idx = 0;
  var stepBtn    = document.getElementById("rf-w1-step");
  var resetBtn   = document.getElementById("rf-w1-reset");
  var progressEl = document.getElementById("rf-w1-progress");
  var explainEl  = document.getElementById("rf-w1-explain");
  var tableEl    = document.getElementById("rf-w1-table");

  var nodeIds = ["q0","q1","q2","q3"];

  function colorNode(id, mode) {
    var g = document.getElementById("rf-node-" + id);
    var circles = g.querySelectorAll("circle");
    if (mode === "new") {
      circles.forEach(function(c) {
        if (c.getAttribute("r") === "28") {
          c.setAttribute("fill", "#fff3b0");
          c.setAttribute("stroke", "#d4860b");
          c.setAttribute("stroke-width", "3");
        } else {
          c.setAttribute("stroke", "#d4860b");
        }
      });
    } else if (mode === "reached") {
      circles.forEach(function(c) {
        if (c.getAttribute("r") === "28") {
          c.setAttribute("fill", "#d4f7ef");
          c.setAttribute("stroke", "#2ec4b6");
          c.setAttribute("stroke-width", "3");
        } else {
          c.setAttribute("stroke", "#2ec4b6");
        }
      });
    } else {
      circles.forEach(function(c) {
        if (c.getAttribute("r") === "28") {
          c.setAttribute("fill", "#e8e8e8");
          c.setAttribute("stroke", "#999");
          c.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2");
        } else {
          c.setAttribute("stroke", "#999");
        }
      });
    }
  }

  function renderTable(rows) {
    tableEl.innerHTML = "";
    rows.forEach(function(row) {
      var tr = document.createElement("tr");
      ["i","r","post","news"].forEach(function(key) {
        var td = document.createElement("td");
        td.textContent = row[key];
        if (row.hl && key !== "i") td.className = "highlight";
        tr.appendChild(td);
      });
      tableEl.appendChild(tr);
    });
  }

  function render() {
    var s = STEPS[idx];
    progressEl.textContent = "Iteration " + idx + " / " + (STEPS.length - 1);
    explainEl.innerHTML = s.explain;
    nodeIds.forEach(function(nid) {
      if (s.newStates.indexOf(nid) >= 0) {
        colorNode(nid, "new");
      } else if (s.reached.indexOf(nid) >= 0) {
        colorNode(nid, "reached");
      } else {
        colorNode(nid, "unreached");
      }
    });
    renderTable(s.tableRows);
    stepBtn.disabled  = idx >= STEPS.length - 1;
    resetBtn.disabled = idx === 0;
  }

  stepBtn.addEventListener("click", function() { if (idx < STEPS.length - 1) { idx++; render(); } });
  resetBtn.addEventListener("click", function() { idx = 0; render(); });
  render();
})();
</script>
```

```{=html}
  });

(function() {

    {
      explain: "<b>Question:</b> Is L(A) = &Sigma;*? Reduction: check whether L(complement(A)) = &empty;.",
      summary: "<b>Reduction:</b><br>L(A) = &Sigma;* &hArr; &Sigma;* &setminus; L(A) = &empty; &hArr; L(complement(A)) = &empty;<br><br>Complement construction: swap accepting and non-accepting states.<br>Original F = {q&#x2083;} &rarr; Complement F&#x0304; = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;}"
    },
    {
      explain: "<b>Step 1 &mdash; Run reachability on complement(A).</b> From Widget 1 we know R* = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;} (all states are reachable).",
      summary: "<b>Reachability:</b><br>R* = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;}<br><br>Same fixpoint as in Widget 1 &mdash; complementation does not change the transition structure."
    },
    {
      explain: "<b>Step 2 &mdash; Check emptiness.</b> R* &cap; F&#x0304; = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;, q&#x2083;} &cap; {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;} = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;} &ne; &empty;.",
      summary: "<b>Emptiness check:</b><br>R* &cap; F&#x0304; = {q&#x2080;, q&#x2081;, q&#x2082;} &ne; &empty;<br><br>&rarr; complement(A) is <b>non-empty</b>"
    },

Reading &lsquo;b&rsquo; from q&#x2080; stays in q&#x2080;, which is accepting in the complement (non-accepting in the original). So <code>b</code> &notin; L(A)."

/* ---- PANEL B: Inclusion ---- */
```

---

## What To Notice

1. **The fixpoint converges in at most |Q| iterations.**
   Here we have 4 states, and the fixpoint is reached in exactly 4 steps
   (iterations 0 through 3 discover one new state each; iteration 4 confirms
   the fixpoint). In general $R_i \subseteq R_{i+1} \subseteq Q$, so the chain
   stabilises after at most $|Q|$ steps.

2. **The iteration discovers states in BFS order from $q_0$.**
   $R_0 = \{q_0\}$, then $q_1$ appears at distance 1, $q_2$ at distance 2,
   $q_3$ at distance 3 -- exactly the breadth-first layers of the transition
   graph. The iteration counter $i$ at which a state first appears equals its
   shortest-path distance from $q_0$, which is why the shortest witness for
   non-emptiness has length 3.

3. **All decision problems reduce to emptiness via closure constructions.**
   Universality uses complementation, inclusion uses product with complement,
   equivalence uses two inclusion checks. The only "engine" is
   $L(\mathcal{A}) \stackrel{?}{=} \varnothing$, which is reachability.

4. **Emptiness itself is just graph reachability.**
   The fixpoint iteration $R_{i+1} = R_i \cup \mathrm{Post}(R_i)$ is a
   standard BFS on the state graph. This is the fundamental algorithm
   underlying model checking: verify a property by exploring the reachable
   state space and checking whether any "bad" (or "accepting") state is
   reachable.
